newsitem.title: USA: New York Senator angered by Swiss comments on Nazis.
newsitem.headline: New York Senator angered by Swiss comments on Nazis.

text.p: New York Republican Sen. Alfonse D'Amato said on Friday he was angered by a statement by a member of the Swiss Parliament who said the nation had no reason to apologise for business dealings with Nazi Germany.

"It is shocking and appalling that even a simple apology for wrongdoing in collaboration with the Nazis during the time of the Holocaust is seen by this member of parliament and a Swiss business leader to be inappropriate," D'Amato said in a statement.

His statement was in reaction to comments made in Zurich by a leading Swiss industrialist and right-wing businessman Christoph Blocher who objected that Swiss contributions to a fund for Holocaust survivors were an admission of guilt. He also wrote to Blocher.

Swiss banks have been accused by Jewish groups of hoarding accounts left by Holocaust victims, and three of the largest banks recently announced they were donating $68 million to start up a fund for survivors. They also encouraged both the government and the private sector to contribute.

Blocher, chairman of the Swiss chemicals company EMS Chemie and a member of parliament, said Switzerland's dealings with Germany were necessary for its survival as a neutral country during the Second World War.

"The trade policy was not false, it was legal, correct and necessary for Switzerland's survival ... I want to send the clear message that reparation or an apology is out of the question," Blocher said.
D'Amato has led efforts to find out what happened to assets placed in Swiss banks by victims of the Holocaust.

"Christoph Blocher's statements are a chilling reminder that some people still don't get it. The world must keep vigilant to insure that we don't lose our capacity for moral outrage, the comments of Mr Blocher not withstanding," he said.
